newsitem.title: UK: FORECAST - UK manufacturing output up but fragile.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - UK manufacturing output up but fragile.

text.p: The most sluggish area of the British economy, manufacturing, probably continued its steady rise in February but sterling's strength means this period of grace is doomed to be short-lived, analysts say.

"Manufacturing output has been on a steady uptrend in recent months, and with business surveys still generally giving positive signals, is likely to contine to expand in coming months," said Salomon Brothers UK economist Michael Saunders.
"The sterling rally really only got going in October or November. We will probably have to wait another three months or so before the impact comes through," he said.

The pound's rise has made exports far more expensive and there are already signs that orders are falling because of the loss of competitiveness. The currency scored a 4-1/2 year high against the mark on Tuesday.
"It is by no means certain that stronger demand at home can continue to compensate fully for the loss of competitiveness in overseas markets," said HSBC UK economist Jonathan Loynes.

But for February at least the picture is less gloomy. The average forecast is a 0.3 percent monthly increase, the same as in January and the year on year prediction is for growth to stay unchanged at 1.6 percent.
The data are scheduled for release by the Office of National Statistics at 0830 GMT (0930 BST) on Wednesday.
Analysts say that lower energy sector output, amid warmer weather and falling oil prices, means that the overall measure of industrial production will register a monthly rise of just 0.2 percent.
The yearly growth rate is expected to have slipped back to 2.1 percent from 2.4.

Salomon's Saunders said the vulnerability of the manufacturing sector, in contrast to the booming service sector, underlines the UK's need for a tightening of fiscal rather than monetary policy to rein in demand.
"A rise in interest rates would be very much second best. We don't need an even higher exchange rate," he said.
Sterling's gains have been spurred on by speculation that the 6.0 percent base interest rate will be increased after the May 1 general election.
